# Tiptap Editor

The Tiptap Editor is a headless, framework-agnostic rich text editor that's customizable and extendable through extensions. Its headless nature means it comes without a set user interface, offering full design freedom (for a jumpstart, see linked [UI templates](#examples-codesandbox-and-ui-templates) below). Tiptap is based on the highly reliable [ProseMirror](https://prosemirror.net/) library.

Tiptap Editor is complemented by the collaboration open-source backend [Hocuspocus](https://github.com/ueberdosis/hocuspocus). Both the Editor and Hocuspocus form the foundation of the [Tiptap Suite](https://tiptap.dev/).

### How does the Tiptap Editor work?

- **Headless Framework:** Tiptap does not rely on a user interface. So there is no need for class overrides or code hacks. If you do need an example UI feel free to browse our [UI templates](#examples-codesandbox-and-ui-templates) linked below.
- **Framework-agnostic:** The Tiptap Editor is designed to work across different frontend frameworks. This means whether you're using Vue, React, or plain JavaScript, Tiptap integrates without compatibility issues.
- **Extension based:** Extensions in Tiptap allow for a tailored editing experience, from simple text styling to advanced features like drag-and-drop block editing. You have the option to choose from over 100 extensions available in the [documentation](ht

candidates.readme_excerpt:
# DeepFilterNet
A Low Complexity Speech Enhancement Framework for Full-Band Audio (48kHz) using on Deep Filtering.

![deepfilternet3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16517898/225623209-a54fea75-ca00-404c-a394-c91d2d1146d2.svg)

For PipeWire integration as a virtual noise suppression microphone look [here](https://github.com/Rikorose/DeepFilterNet/blob/main/ladspa/README.md).

### Demo

https://github.com/Rikorose/DeepFilterNet/assets/16517898/79679fd7-de73-4c22-948c-891927c7d2ca

To run the demo (linux only) use:
```bash
cargo +nightly run -p df-demo --features ui --bin df-demo --release
```

### News

- New DeepFilterNet Demo: *DeepFilterNet: Perceptually Motivated Real-Time Speech Enhancement*
  - Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.08227
  - Video: https://youtu.be/EO7n96YwnyE

- New Multi-Frame Filtering Paper: *Deep Multi-Frame Filtering for Hearing Aids*
  - Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.08225

- Real-time version and a LADSPA plugin
  - [Pre-compiled binary](#deep-filter), no python dependencies. Usage: `deep-filter audio-file.wav`
  - [LADSPA plugin](ladspa/) with pipewire filter-chain integration for real-time noise reduction on your mic.

- DeepFilterNet2 Paper: *DeepFilterNet2: Towards Real-Time Speech Enhancement on Embedded Devices for Full-Band Audio*
  - Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.05474
  - Samples: https://rikorose.github.io/DeepFilterNet2-Samples/
  - Demo: https://huggingface.co/spaces/hshr/DeepFilterNet2

- Original DeepFilterNet Paper: *DeepFilterNet: A Low Complexity Speech Enhancement Framework for Full-Band Audio based on Deep Filtering*
  - Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.05588
  - Samples: https://rikorose.github.io/DeepFilterNet-Samples/
  - Demo: https://huggingface.co/spaces/hshr/DeepFilterNet
  - Video Lecture: https://youtu.be/it90gBqkY6k

## Usage

### deep-filter

Download a pre-compiled deep-filter binary from the [release page](https://github.com/Rikorose/DeepFilterNet/releases/).
You can use `deep-filter` to suppress noise in noisy .wav audio files. Currently, only wav files with a sampling rate of 48kHz are supported.

```bash
USAGE:
    deep-filter [OPTIONS] [FILES]...

ARGS:
    <FILES>...

OPTIONS:
    -D, --compensate-delay
            Compensate delay of STFT and model lookahead
    -h, --help
            Print help information
    -m, --model <MODEL>
            Path to model tar.gz. Defaults to DeepFilterNet2.
    -o, --out-dir <OUT_DIR>
            [default: out]
    --pf
            Enable p

Make the scene first. Then make it a video.
Open source previs in a browser tab: block the set, move the cast, cut the camera, hand the shot to an AI video model.

Try it in the browser · Quick start · Guide for AI agents · Docs · Changelog · Discord

Top: the greybox blocked in CozyClay. Bottom: the AI video made from it. Same idea, a parkour jump: the blocking holds the timing and the camera.
## Why AI video costs money per take, and one miss means paying again. A text prompt cannot hold a whole scene: where everyone stands, how they move, where the camera is, when it cuts. CozyClay lets you make those decisions first, in 3D, where they are cheap to change. Then the video model gets the shot as a first frame, a greybox reference clip and a prompt that describes the real framing. It follows the blocking instead of guessing. ```mermaid flowchart LR S["Stage
set + cast"] --> M["Motion
compiled + QA"] --> C["Camera
shots + cuts"] --> E["Export
frame · clip · prompt"] --> V["AI video model"] ``` ## Quick start

candidates.readme_excerpt:
# VoxCanvas Data Pipeline **VoxCanvas-41M: A Large-Scale Bilingual Dataset for Instruction-Based Speech Editing and Its Learning Dynamics** [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Page-blue?logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://zhikangniu.github.io/voxcanvas) [![Paper](https://img.shields.io/badge/Paper-arXiv-b31b1b?logo=arxiv&logoColor=white)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08251) [![Dataset](https://img.shields.io/badge/Dataset-VoxCanvas--41M-ffcc4d?logo=huggingface&logoColor=black)](https://huggingface.co/datasets/zkniu/VoxCanvas) [![Code License](https://img.shields.io/badge/Code_License-MIT-green)](LICENSE)
VoxCanvas-41M has about 41M Chinese and English speech-editing pairs, each a source utterance, a text instruction and the edited utterance. This repository builds its **content-editing** part (single-span, multi-span and location-reference editing) from real speech (Emilia) in five stages: 0. **align**: Qwen3-ASR-1.7B re-transcription and Qwen3-ForcedAligner-0.6B word timestamps; 1. **annotate**: rule-based edit selection, LLM-generated new words and instruction templates; 2. **synthesize**: F5-TTS masked infilling of the edited regions; 3. **verify**: ASR (zero WER / tone-pinyin error) and speaker-similarity checks; 4. **export**: the final pairs. The algorithms, data formats and every difference from the released data are documented in [docs/pipeline.md](docs/pipeline.md). ## Repository layout ``` src/voxcanvas/ align.py stage 0: ASR transcript + forced alignment annotate/ stage 1 (python -m voxcanvas.annotate) __main__.py CLI: gate -> candidates -> sampling -> LLM completion -> records content.py single_span (deletion, insertion, substitution) and multi_span occurrence.py repeated words: d1 d4 m1 m2 i1 i2 boundary.py sentence head / tail: l_d l_m l_i timestamp.py time point / interval: l_t_d l_t_m l_t_i templates.py instruction templates (zh / en) prompts.py LLM prompts llm.py OpenAI-compatible client, LLM replacement / insertion generation records.py edit record, length-stratified sampling text.py tokenizers, alignment gate, edit application, validators synthesize.py stage 2: F5-TTS edit synthesis verify/asr.py stage 3a: ASR check verify/sim.py stage 3b: speaker similarity

candidates.description: Sub-50mb agentic, voice and vision intelligence for consumer devices.
candidates.readme_excerpt:
![Cactus Compute - Sub-50mb Super Intelligence For Consumer Devices](assets/banner.svg)

Run text, speech and vision models locally with one Python package. Cactus provides tool calling, structured extraction, transcription, image understanding and model fine-tuning.

## Install

```sh
pip install -U cactus-compute
```

Python 3.9 or later. The package downloads and caches the engine and requested model weights on first use. Inference runs locally and does not require JAX.

## Agents

[Needle 3](https://cactuscompute.com/needle) calls tools, extracts structured data and embeds text.

```python
import cactus

@cactus.tool
def get_weather(city: str):
    "Get the current weather for a city."
    return {"city": city, "temp_c": 27, "sky": "clear"}

with cactus.Cactus(tools=[get_weather]) as agent:
    print(agent.run("What's the weather in Lagos?")["results"])
```

`run()` executes your functions and returns their results. Use `complete()` when you want to inspect the proposed calls before executing them.

## Voice

[Whistle](https://cactuscompute.com/blog/whistle) transcribes speech in seven languages, with word timestamps and speech embeddings.

```python
import cactus

print(cactus.transcribe("clip.wav")["text"])
```

Use a 16 kHz WAV file. Install `cactus-compute[mic]` for other sample rates or microphone capture.

## Vision

[Mirage](https://huggingface.co/Cactus-Compute/mirage) describes images and extracts structured data.

```python
import cactus

print(cactus.Mirage().describe("photo.png"))
```

## Documentation

- [Python API and CLI](https://cactuscompute.com/blog/needle-python-docs)
- [Runtime binaries and supported platforms](https://huggingface.co/Cactus-Compute/cactus)
- [Fine-tune Needle](https://cactuscompute.com/blog/finetuning-needle) or [Whistle](https://cactuscompute.com/blog/finetuning-whistle) with `cactus-compute[train]`
- [Reference for coding assistants](llms.txt)

Migrating from `cactus-needle`? Use `import cactus` and the `cactus` command. Needle 2 remains on the [legacy branch](https://github.com/cactus-compute/cactus/tree/legacy) with `cactus-compute<4`. The earlier general inference SDK is now [cactus-engine](https://pypi.org/project/cactus-engine/).

Anonymous Python usage counts can be disabled with `CACTUS_TELEMETRY=0`. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for the Apache 2.0 license.

candidates.description: Open-source generative UI framework: agents stream layout data, and apps render it with native components in React, Angular, Lit, Flutter, SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose.
candidates.readme_excerpt: # A2UI: Agent-to-User Interface A2UI is an open-source generative UI framework, complete with a format optimized for representing updatable agent-generated UIs and an initial set of renderers, that allows agents to generate or populate rich user interfaces. _A gallery of A2UI rendered cards, showing a variety of UI compositions that A2UI can achieve._ ## Summary Generative AI excels at creating text and code, but agents can struggle to present rich, interactive interfaces to users, especially when those agents are remote or running across trust boundaries. **A2UI** is an open standard and set of libraries that allows agents to "speak UI." Agents send a declarative JSON format describing the _intent_ of the UI. The client application then renders this using its own native component library (Flutter, Angular, Lit, etc.). This approach ensures that agent-generated UIs are **safe like data, but expressive like code**. ## When to use A2UI - **Use A2UI** when you need agent-generated UI on **Flutter**, **Angular**, **SwiftUI / Jetpack Compose**, or **more than one platform** from the same agent. - **Use A2UI** when the agent is **remote, third-party, or across a trust boundary** and must not send executable code to your renderer. - **Use A2UI on Flutter** with [`a2ui_flutter`](dart/a2ui_flutter/): `flutter pub add a2ui_flutter a2ui_core`. It replaces the `genui` package. - **You may not need A2UI** for a **React-only chat** that renders tool results as your own components; an LLM toolkit alone may be enough. A2UI fits once you add platforms or remote agents. Install the renderer for your framework, for example `npm install @a2ui/react` (or `@a2ui/angular`, `@a2ui/lit`). It depends on `@a2ui/web_core`; add `@a2ui/web_core` explicitly too if your app imports from it directly (e.g. the message processor or basic catalog). See the [Client Setup guide](https://a2ui.org/guides/client-setup/) for each platform. ## High-level philosophy A2UI was designed to address the specific challenges of interoperable, cross-platform, generative or template-based UI responses from agents. The project's core philosophies: - **Security first**: Running arbitrary code generated by an LLM may present a security risk. A2UI is a declarative data format, not executable code. Your client application maintains a "catalog" of trusted, pre-approved UI components

ChatGPT 现在能直接做 GIF，但一张一张做，形象容易跑，尺寸也不是微信要的。这个 skill 把剩下的事都做了：

- 一个参考图锁定整套角色
- 240×240 GIF，自动压到 500KB 以内
- 封面、图标、横幅、赞赏图一起出
- 按微信规范自动检查
- 上架文案和给客户的交付包

## 安装

把这个文件夹放进你的 Agent 的 skills 目录，比如：

```bash
git clone https://github.com/imraywang/ray-sticker-shop ~/.claude/skills/ray-sticker-shop
```

然后对 Claude Code 或 Codex 说：「把这张猫的照片做成一套表情包。」

## 需要什么

- Python 3.9+ 和 Pillow：`pip install pillow`
- `OPENAI_API_KEY`（中转站再设 `OPENAI_BASE_URL`）
- 没有 key 也行：Agent 会给你提示词，到 ChatGPT 里出图，放回来照样合成

## 花费

8 张表情加 5 张配套素材，按 OpenAI 官方单价约 $0.7，重抽另算。实际花费记录在项目目录的 `costs.jsonl`。

## 注意

只做你有权使用的形象。微信不收未授权的二创和同人。过审由微信决定，本工具不保证过审和收入。

Given a production-level website they can explore through a browser, agents must reverse-engineer a full-stack version that matches its appearance and behavior as closely as possible. ## Tasks 70 websites and 46,916 hidden test cases, on [Harbor Hub](https://hub.harborframework.com/datasets/websitebench/WebsiteBench) and [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/TIGER-Lab/WebsiteBench). See the [task list](docs/tasks.md).
